items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: A few weeks after I started with Johnny, he hired a trombone player named Herb Gregory.

ctx.x: A few weeks after I started with Johnny, he hired a trombone player named Herb Gregory. Herb had come up in the music game with Rex Stewart and was a great admirer of Jimmy Harrison and I got a good idea of how Jimmy had played from listening to Herb. He had the worst looking teeth of any horn blower that I ever saw. They were snagged and looked as though they were going to fall out at any moment, but when he put his horn to his mouth and started to play, the sounds that came from his horn were unbelievable.

Herb had not been working much before he joined Monnegue, so the first week with us Ted and I shared our bottle with him and he promised to bring in a bottle after he had received a week's pay. There were no nights off in ballrooms or dancing schools and at this place we were paid every Sunday night. Neither Ted nor I brought in a bottle on Monday night because Herb was supposed to bring one. After we played a few numbers Herb brought out his bottle and passed it to me. I took a taste and almost brought up my…
the gutter and it tasted as if it could be embalming fluid, if embalming fluid has a taste.
